# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Mute. I hold the defusal manual, which states:
1. Press the key with symbol ᖉ first (any wrong touch detonates the bomb).
2. Look at the light below it to determine the wire to cut:
   - Blue light -> cut blue wire
   - Green light -> cut red wire
   - Yellow light -> cut yellow wire

I cannot speak, only gesture. Deaf can see gestures and can speak out loud to both Blind and me. Deaf cannot hear.
Blind cannot see gestures or the bomb, but can hear speech and manipulate the bomb.

Since Deaf has not yet spoken to describe what keys are on the bomb or establish a gesture code ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"), any gesture I send now would have no agreed meaning. Blind must also not touch anything until Deaf identifies the key and instructs Blind.

I will wait for Deaf to observe the bomb, speak to us, describe the candidate keys/markings, and establish a signaling system.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a display, a light, keypad slots 1 to 4 expecting 1 digit, and wires 1 to 3.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display is 0. Indicator light is green. Wires 1 to 3: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. Keypad needs 1 digit. Button 1: backwards letter d, or upside-down letter P. Button 2: butterfly or hourglass shape with vertical lines inside. Button 3: three dots stacked vertically. Button 4: trident, pitchfork, or cactus shape. Mute, please gesture to me what Blind needs to do.

I need to inform Deaf that Button 1 (which wears the symbol ᖉ, described by Deaf as a backwards d / upside-down P) is the correct button to press first. Deaf specifically enumerated the buttons 1 to 4 and noted the keypad needs 1 digit.

Using the gesture alphabet, `☝` clearly signals the number 1 (Button 1).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, do not touch the bomb yet! Mute, you signalled 1, but we have both Wire 1 and Keypad Button 1. Please clarify: gesture thumbs up if you mean cut Wire 1, or gesture thumbs down if you mean press Keypad Button 1.

I need to clarify Deaf's question. Deaf asked:
"gesture thumbs up if you mean cut Wire 1, or gesture thumbs down if you mean press Keypad Button 1."

The manual explicitly states to press the key that wears ᖉ first (which is Keypad Button 1). Therefore, I should gesture thumbs down (`👎`).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, press keypad button 1. Mute, after this action, please gesture our next step if needed.

I should wait for Blind to press keypad button 1 and for Deaf to observe any changes to the indicator light before signaling the next step.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: the keypad opens
Blind says to Mute: Pressed keypad button 1.
Deaf says: The keypad opened successfully! Wires remain: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. Indicator light is green, display is 0. Mute, what should Blind do next? Gesture 1, 2, or 3 for wire to cut, or a thumbs up if we are done.

I need to tell Deaf which wire Blind should cut.

The defusal manual specifies:
- Green light -> cut red wire.

From Deaf's report:
- Indicator light is green.
- Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.

Therefore, Blind must cut Wire 1 (the red wire). Deaf asked to "Gesture 1, 2, or 3 for wire to cut". I will gesture `☝` to indicate Wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, cut wire 1, which is the first wire (the red wire).

I will wait for Blind to cut wire 1.

```
wait()
```
